prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer in Dallas for every truck accident — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case, the lawyer’s specific trucking experience, resources, and whether you want a trial lawyer or a settlement-focused attorney.

I can help you find the best lawyer for your situation. Below are practical steps and what to look for when choosing a truck-accident attorney in Dallas.

What to look for (must-haves)
- Substantial truck-accident experience (not just general PI). Trucking cases involve FMCSA/DOT rules, logbooks, ELD/black box data, and multiple potentially liable parties (driver, carrier, broker, maintenance company).
- Trial experience and a record of verdicts/large settlements in truck cases.
- Resources to hire experts (accident reconstruction, medical, economic loss) and to advance case costs.
- Track record handling catastrophic injuries and wrongful death (if applicable).
- Good client communication and responsiveness.
- Contingency-fee agreement (typical for PI): confirm percentage and whether expenses are deducted before/after your portion.
- Positive client reviews and peer recognition (Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, state bar discipline check).

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many in Dallas/Fort Worth?
- What were some results (settlements/verdicts) for truck cases?
- Do you have experience with FMCSA/DOT regulations, ELD/black box data, and accident reconstruction?
- Will you handle my case personally or hand it to another attorney/staff?
- How do you charge (contingency percent, costs, medical liens)?
- Do you have the resources to take the case to trial if needed?
- Can you provide references from past clients (or online reviews)?

Documents to bring to a consultation
- Police report
- Photos/video of the scene and vehicles
- Medical records and bills, ER notes
- Insurance information (your own and others)
- Names/contacts of witnesses
- Any correspondence with insurers

Where to find and verify candidates
- Texas State Bar website (attorney lookup for license & discipline)
- SuperLawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell
- Local PI firms’ websites (look for trucking specialization)
- Google/Avvo reviews and verdict databases
- Recommendations from local medical providers or other attorneys

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific money amount
- No trucking-specific experience
- Pushy “sign now” tactics for no clear reason
- Poor reviews citing non-communication or missed deadlines

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft a short message/email to send to prospective lawyers;
- Give a prioritized list of questions for your first 3 consultations;
- If you share your Dallas ZIP code and more about your case (injuries, crash date), I can suggest what types of firms to call and how to narrow choices.

Which would you like to do next?
